research_mode: official Home Office, Police.uk and Office for Statistics Regulation web sources only; current 2025-26 outcomes release, outcome-framework versioning, table revision and missing-data semantics, date-specific category dictionaries and end-to-end quality-assurance boundaries; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Crime outcomes in England and Wales 2025 to 2026
verified_claims: published 23 July 2026
covers the financial year ending March 2026
separates outcomes assigned to offences recorded to March 2025 from total outcomes recorded
limitations: the two views have different cohort semantics

sources.name: Crime outcomes 2025 to 2026 bulletin
verified_claims: the current outcomes framework began in April 2013
it replaced the narrower detections framework
framework changes affect historical comparability
limitations: pre-framework series require a version break

sources.name: Technical annex Crimsec4 additional collections
verified_claims: outcomes 20 to 22 are absent from Crimsec4 forms
five transfer or cancellation subcategories are also absent
these fields use an additional manual quarterly collection
limitations: manual collection has different timing and controls

sources.name: Open-data user guide Outcome 1A
verified_claims: Outcome 1A is charge or summons for an alternative offence
introduced voluntarily in April 2016
the relevant new outcomes became mandatory in April 2017

sources.name: Open-data user guide Outcome 22
verified_claims: Outcome 22 covers diversionary educational or intervention activity
voluntary from April 2019
compulsory from April 2021
limitations: early local use may be inconsistent
cross-break comparison needs a version flag

sources.name: Home Office Crime Recording Rules
verified_claims: provides the national standard for recording notifiable offences
page updated 16 July 2026
the update attached revised outcomes-framework guidance
limitations: publication does not prove uniform force application

sources.name: PRC open-data geography scope
verified_claims: tables publish PFA and CSP figures
BTP is excluded from CSP data
CSP totals need not equal national totals
limitations: PFA and CSP are not LSOA or parcel levels

sources.name: Open-data guide offence code 49A
verified_claims: 49A became separate in April 2013
a 2002/03 to 2012/13 back series was created
the series mixes actual and estimated data
limitations: estimated and submitted values must be distinguished

sources.name: Open-data guide burglary classifications
verified_claims: burglary classification changed in April 2017
residential and non-residential replaced domestic and non-domestic
new residential subcategories began in April 2023
limitations: classification eras are not automatically comparable

sources.name: Linked-quarter outcomes method
verified_claims: one view links outcomes to offences recorded in the quarter
open investigations are included
first publication is incomplete and matures over time

sources.name: Outcomes open-data publication design
verified_claims: two outcome views have existed since 2014/15
updates have been quarterly since October 2015
the views answer different questions
limitations: denominators cannot be shared without cohort alignment
quarterly cadence is not monthly completeness

sources.name: Supplementary metrics missing-data contract
verified_claims: empty can mean suppressed due to low volumes
empty can mean no data to calculate
empty can mean data not available

sources.name: Supplementary metric precision and revision contract
verified_claims: metrics are correct at extraction time
values are subject to future revisions
values are published without rounding
limitations: display rounding must not replace source precision

sources.name: PRC additivity contract
verified_claims: figures are additive within defined dimensions
four quarters can form a 12-month PFA total
CSP totals need not reconcile nationally
limitations: source values must not be altered to force reconciliation

sources.name: PRC quarterly revision contract
verified_claims: records may later be transferred or cancelled
quarterly figures are revised every quarter
historical extracts can change

sources.name: Open-data revision history
verified_claims: March 2022 outcomes data were corrected to remove duplicate lines on 5 August 2025
2021/22 supplementary metrics were revised
the page records dated table-family updates
limitations: download success does not identify the corrected edition

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Crime categories API contract
verified_claims: categories are returned for a specified dataset date
url is the category identifier
name is the human-readable label
limitations: one month's dictionary is not universal

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: All-crime category semantics
verified_claims: all-crime is named All crime and ASB
ASB is also a separate category
identifier and label are separate
limitations: all-crime is not only notifiable crime
it is not an IoD Crime Domain substitute

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Forces and BTP scope contracts
verified_claims: the forces endpoint lists API forces
BTP is excluded from that list
crime responses can separately use a BTP location type
limitations: force IDs are not ONS geography codes

sources.name: Home Office QA cadence
verified_claims: monthly QA uses logic and consistency checks
quarterly reconciliation is more detailed
the stages are distinct
limitations: logic checks do not prove recording completeness

sources.name: Accuracy assurance boundary
verified_claims: Home Office checks include completeness consistency and validity
submitted data cannot show whether crimes were recorded when required
HMICFRS audits estimate recording accuracy
limitations: inspection evidence is not parcel evidence

sources.name: HMICFRS inspection timing
verified_claims: inspections sample crimes from the most recent three months
forces are inspected roughly every three to five years
between-inspection accuracy is not continuously observed
limitations: old results are not current record accuracy

sources.name: Automated QA controls
verified_claims: some forces use robotic QA tools
analysts monitor outputs and retain manual contingencies
OSR warns against ignoring root causes
limitations: not every force uses the same controls

sources.name: 2023 Counting Rules changes
verified_claims: Counting Rules had a major 2023 review
a 2017 multi-recording requirement was reversed
a principal-crime rule generally applies with stated exceptions
limitations: other harmful behaviour may still exist

sources.name: Recommendation 8
verified_claims: ONS should expand quality information
coverage should include force QA arrangements
coverage should include IT limitations and improvements since 2014
limitations: recommendation is not proof of completion

sources.name: Recommendation 10
verified_claims: ONS HMICFRS Home Office and forces should investigate divergence drivers
PRC and CSEW have different measurement bases
the sources have different strengths and limitations
limitations: sources must not be merged into parcel certainty
